entry.idea: Salespeople spend a lot of their day on notes, CRM updates and follow-up messages instead of selling, so Convo built an AI copilot that helps them handle that work faster.
entry.lesson: Pick one repetitive, high-volume task inside a job almost everyone already has, like sales note-taking and follow-up, and build an AI assistant focused only on that task.
entry.name: Convo

growth.reason: No user numbers, revenue or funding were found; the only trace is a single Product Hunt launch listing.

market.reason: Every business with a sales team, in any country, could use a tool like this, so the potential market is large even though the space is crowded.

tech.reason: An 'AI copilot for salespeople' sounds like a layer built on top of existing AI models and CRMs, which many competitors could copy quickly.

sources.title: Convo - An AI copilot for salespeople

entry.twist: Public information does not go far past a short Product Hunt listing, and the name is shared by several unrelated companies (an ASL interpreting service, an older workspace-chat company, and others), so what makes this particular Convo different is not documented yet.
entry.who_pays: Sales teams and the companies that employ them would be the ones paying for the software, though no confirmed customers or pricing are public yet.
entry.why_now: AI tools have gotten good enough to draft messages, summarize calls and update records on their own, which is exactly the kind of routine writing and admin work that used to eat up a salesperson's day.
